newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Prairie harvest 2-3 weeks from complete.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Prairie harvest 2-3 weeks from complete.

text.p: Canada's Prairie harvest was expected to take another two to three weeks to complete due to rain and snow delays, Pioneer Grain Co Ltd said in a crop report for the week ended October 2.

British Columbia's Dawson Creek region and Alberta's Peace River Valley were at least three weeks away from completing harvest with about 10 to 15 percent combined to date. Snow and heavy frosts were reported across the region.
Alberta's harvest was two weeks from being complete. Overall, 50 percent of crops were combined. Southern Alberta was most advanced with 90 percent harvested.
Northwest Saskatchewan combined 40 percent of crops, swathed 90 percent. Harvest should be done in two to three weeks. The region saw one to eight inches of snow.
North central Saskatchewan swathed 95 percent of crops, combined 55 percent of barley and canola, 50 percent of wheat, 40 percent of oats and durum and five percent of flax.
Northeast Saskatchewan combined 80 percent of wheat and oats, 50 percent of barley and canola but no flax. Overnight temperatures of -8.0 Celsius (17.6 F) should downgrade crops.
Southwest Saskatchewan saw an average 3.5 inches of rain and snow and harvest should take another two weeks.

Southeast Saskatchewan saw one foot of snow in some areas and an average of 3.5 inches of snow. Wheat and durum were 45 percent combined, canola and barley were 70 percent done, oats were 55 percent harvested and flax was 35 percent combined.
Eastern Saskatchewan and Manitoba made little harvest progress in the past week. The region saw an average of one inch in precipitation. Harvest should take at least two weeks.
